evaluations.rationale: No other story imposes an incompatible permission, behavior, constraint, or rule with viewing a list of sponsors.
No conflicting story restricts anonymous users from viewing user profiles or imposes incompatible rules.
No other story imposes incompatible permissions or behaviors for emailing trainers from the website.
No other story conflicts with providing a clear map of buildings and rooms.
No other story imposes an incompatible permission that would prevent trainers from editing their training node themselves.
No other story requires or enables multiple registrations per day for an authenticated user, so the one-per-day constraint is not contradicted.
No conflicting story restricts training coordinators from having an admin view to track registration status.
No other story imposes rules incompatible with adding an attendee to a training waitlist.
Requiring acceptance of cancellation terms via checkbox does not conflict with other stories' behaviors or constraints.
Tying a cancellation deadline into registration/cancellation workflows does not conflict with other backlog items.
Adding to 'my schedule' if a schedule exists is not contradicted by any other story.
Viewing which trainings a user has signed up for does not conflict with other requirements.
Allowing trainers to see class attendance (trusted with privacy) is not contradicted by any story that forbids trainer access to this information.
An admin view for training coordinators showing trainee info and filters is not inconsistent with other stories.
Creating dedicated training pages with the listed details and SEO-friendly paths does not conflict with other stories.
Displaying training options clearly with the specified fields does not introduce incompatibilities with other backlog items.
A training landing page with intro section and list of offerings does not conflict with other requirements.
Linking from the home page to training options does not conflict with other stories.
Providing information about the coding lounge and hours does not conflict with other items.
Administrator refunding sponsorship money via Stripe is consistent with payment and refund related stories.
Providing a link for authenticated users to become a $350 sponsor does not conflict with other stories.
Allowing anonymous users to see attendees associated with a company is not contradicted elsewhere.
Authenticated users identifying and paying for a $350 company sponsorship is consistent with payment flows and other stories.
Administrators creating and maintaining venues does not conflict with any other permissions or constraints.
Anonymous users viewing venue details is not contradicted by other stories.
Showing sessions associated with sponsor attendees to anonymous users does not conflict with other items.
Displaying a payment page as part of registration for authenticated users is consistent with other payment stories.
Administrators assigning sponsors to events and features is not in conflict with other stories.
Anonymous users seeing all events a sponsor is sponsoring is compatible with other requirements.
Authenticated users entering payment information and being charged is consistent with refund and payment stories.
A sponsor linking attendees to their sponsorship page does not impose incompatible behavior with other stories.
Authenticated users updating their profile is not in conflict with other requirements.
Anonymous users signing up for the newsletter does not contradict other stories.
Administrators tagging blog posts for Drupal Planet is not incompatible with any other story.
Administrators creating blog posts is consistent with content authoring requirements and poses no conflicts.
Anonymous users reading the blog does not contradict any other story.

Summit coordinator listing an agenda is not incompatible with other backlog items.
Showing how many seats are left for a summit to anonymous users does not conflict with other stories.
Providing specific summit details to anonymous users is compatible with other requirements.
Listing all summits for anonymous users is not contradicted elsewhere.
Anonymous users learning about sponsorship levels does not conflict with other items.
Offering a WYSIWYG for authenticated users is consistent with other content-editing stories and not contradictory.
